title: B200 bring-up checklist (early fleet): compatibility gate, benchmark subset, rollback plan
creator: Talia Benson
related_links: GitHub (runtime): PR-24927 B200 provisional SKU detection + compatibility gate
GitHub (benchmark-lab): PR-927 B200 smoke suite (allowed-to-fail initially)
body:
Context
- We are onboarding early B200 nodes into benchmark-lab + limited Hosted canary pools.
- Goal is to avoid “silent bad defaults” and make B200 performance/stability observable and reversible.

Scope / deliverable
1) Compatibility gate (hard checks + explicit override path)
2) B200 benchmark subset (“smoke suite” + minimal matrix) with acceptance thresholds appropriate for bring-up
3) Rollback plan (kill-switch semantics + operational steps) for Hosted and for Dedicated opt-in

Non-goals
- Full B200 optimization / final defaults (that is expected-behavior-b200-preview + follow-up tuning work)
- Replacing Infra’s driver standardization work; we just need to safely handle variance during early fleet.

(1) Compatibility gate checklist
Required detection inputs (runtime)
- GPU SKU detection: identify B200 reliably (incl. PCI IDs / NVML name variants).
- Driver version: major.minor.patch (minimum supported + denylist known-bad).
- CUDA runtime/toolkit version (container)
- Optional but strongly recommended: PCIe vs SXM (if detectable), MIG mode (expected off for B200 early fleet), HBM size if vendor variations appear.

Hard gate behavior (default)
- If SKU=B200 and runtime cannot match a supported compatibility entry for the requested profile pack version:
  - Refuse to start serving (fail closed) for Hosted pools and benchmark-lab runners.
  - For Private installs: start but log WARN + surface “unsupported” in /health and Console; do not auto-select B200 defaults.
- If SKU=B200 and profile_version is not explicitly pinned:
  - Refuse to auto-select B200 profile. Require profile_version pin OR explicit allow_early_access_b200=true (guardrail flag).

Explicit override path (escape hatch)
- Allow a “break glass” runtime flag (gated by environment / RBAC in control plane) to proceed despite compatibility mismatch:
  - runtime.config.allow_unsupported_hardware=true
  - Must emit audit log + tag all metrics with compatibility_status=unsupported
  - Must page on-call if enabled in Hosted.

Compatibility matrix requirements (what goes into the profile pack)
- A single source of truth mapping:
  - sku=B200
  - min_driver_version
  - supported_driver_ranges (or denylist)
  - min_cuda_version
  - profile_ids allowed for B200 (provisional)
- Versioning: compatibility matrix is versioned with the profile pack (not the runtime binary), but runtime must enforce the gate.

Owner notes
- Quentin: define matrix format + validation rules.
- Ethan Park / Benji: wire “break glass” + audit log hook into control plane config paths.

(2) Benchmark matrix subset (B200 smoke suite)
Goal
- Establish “is it healthy?” signals before we chase absolute best performance.

Suite definition (benchmark-lab)
- Models (representative, already in our perf harness):
  - 7B-class dense (prefill heavy)
  - 13B-class dense (mixed)
  - 70B-class dense (decode heavy) OR the smallest 70B variant we can run within early HBM constraints
- Workload buckets:
  - Short prompts / short outputs (chat-like): prompt 128–512, output 128–512
  - Long prompt / short output (RAG-ish): prompt 2k–8k, output 128–256
  - Short prompt / long output (agentic): prompt 256–512, output 1k–2k
- Concurrency points (keep small initially to reduce noise): 1, 4, 8 (and 16 only if memory headroom stable)
- Quantization: run one FP16/BF16 config + one common quant profile we use in Hosted (Arjun to confirm which is most representative).

Metrics to capture (must-have)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, plus stage breakdown (queue_ms, prefill_ms, decode_ms)
- Throughput: tokens/sec (prefill + decode), requests/sec
- GPU: util %, SM occupancy proxy, HBM used / free
- Stability: OOM count, CUDA error count, kernel fallback rate, allocator fragmentation estimate, KV compaction time

Bring-up acceptance thresholds (initial; tuned once we have 3+ clean runs)
- Correctness: output determinism within expected tolerance (same seeds), no schema/format regressions in structured output tests.
- Stability:
  - OOM = 0 across the suite
  - CUDA errors = 0
  - kernel_fallback_rate < 0.5% for supported shapes; if >0.5% require investigation + explicit annotation in results.
- Performance (relative):
  - No worse than H100 baseline by >20% on end-to-end p99 for the same workload bucket when run in a controlled environment.
  - If worse, must be explained via known gating factors (driver/CUDA mismatch, kernel disablement) and tracked as a follow-up.

Run discipline
- Minimum 3 runs per configuration; report median.
- Run ordering randomized to reduce thermal/neighbor noise.
- Record: profile_pack_version, profile_id, git sha, driver, cuda, instance type, region.

(3) Rollback plan
Hosted
- Kill-switch: disable profile pack default selection for B200 pools (force legacy defaults) OR force a known-good profile_id.
- Rollback trigger gates (align with SRE):
  - p99 latency regression >10% sustained for 15m in canary cohort
  - error rate (5xx + model execution errors) >0.5% for 10m
  - kernel fallback rate >2% for 10m (unless annotated as expected for a specific canary test)
  - any OOM spike above baseline
- Rollback steps (operational)
  1) Flip feature flag to disable B200 profile selection
  2) Drain canary pool / cordon nodes
  3) Revert to previous runtime build if needed (runtime-1.22.0 -> runtime-1.21.x), but prefer config rollback first
  4) Attach incident template + postmortem follow-ups (metrics gaps, gate tightening)

Dedicated (opt-in only for early access)
- Customers must pin profile_version and acknowledge “early access B200” support boundaries.
- Rollback = customer pin to prior profile_version OR disable early access flag.
- Provide support playbook snippet for CSE/Solutions: what to request from customer (driver/CUDA, profile_version, /health debug bundle).

Private
- Installer should warn on unsupported driver/CUDA combos and recommend pinning profile_version.
- Rollback is customer-controlled: Helm values revert + restart; ensure docs include exact values.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Runtime refuses to run B200 defaults unless a compatible profile pack version is present (fail closed for Hosted + benchmark-lab).
- [ ] Control-plane supports a break-glass override with audit logging, and metrics are tagged compatibility_status=unsupported when used.
- [ ] benchmark-lab has B200 smoke suite runner producing artifacts tagged with profile_version + compatibility metadata.
- [ ] SRE-approved rollback triggers + steps documented (link from rollout plan ENG-4933).
- [ ] Confluence expected-behavior-b200-preview updated with the above gates + what to watch.

Open questions
- Do we require CUDA minor version exact-match (e.g., 12.4.x) or allow a range? Infra preference is to standardize, but early fleet exceptions likely.
- How strict should “fail closed” be for Dedicated? Proposal: default to warn + refuse auto-select, but allow explicit pin.

Follow-ups (likely separate tickets)
- Tighten B200 performance thresholds once we have stable baselines.
- Add more workload shapes (long-context extreme) once kernels stabilize.
- Expand compatibility detection to include SXM/PCIe and HBM size variants if they show up in fleet.
comments: 2026-01-17 — Talia Benson (PM): Marking this P0 for runtime-1.22 bring-up. We need a clear definition of “fail closed” vs “warn” per deployment mode. Please sync with Neha/Sean before finalizing gate semantics.

2026-01-24 — Quentin Harris: Drafted compatibility matrix format proposal: sku + driver_range + cuda_range + required_profile_pack_version. Planning to implement validation as part of ENG-4922, but this ticket will define B200-specific policy (require explicit pin).

2026-02-02 — Neha Kapoor (Infra/SRE sponsor): Early B200 nodes are not fully standardized yet. We will have at least 2 driver versions in the wild for ~2–3 weeks. Strong preference: runtime should refuse to run “B200 auto defaults” unless it matches a supported range, but allow break-glass for benchmark-lab only. For Hosted, fail closed is fine as long as pool management can cordon nodes cleanly.

2026-02-06 — Rina Kobayashi (Benchmark harness): I can add a B200 smoke suite in benchmark-lab. Need final list of models + prompt/response distributions by Feb 12 to land with PR-927. Also: please ensure results store profile_version + driver/cuda tags, otherwise we can’t compare runs.

2026-02-10 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): Rollback triggers look reasonable. Suggest adding an explicit OOM trigger: any non-zero OOM in canary is immediate rollback. Also, kernel fallback alert should be tiered: warn at 1%, page at 2% sustained 10m (unless canary is intentionally testing fallback paths).

2026-02-12 — Quentin Harris: Incorporated Infra driver baseline thread notes. Proposed rule: for sku=B200, require profile_version pin in all modes; Hosted additionally requires compatibility match (no break-glass except benchmark-lab). Will route to Mateo for final sign-off.

2026-02-19 — Hiro Tanaka (Kernel): One more metric request for smoke suite: log attention_kernel_choice + fallback_reason counts. We saw driver mismatches manifest as silent fallback to slower kernels; need it in acceptance report.

2026-02-22 — Quentin Harris: Status update: compatibility gate implementation mostly in runtime PR-24927; working with Ethan/Benji on audit log + break-glass wiring. Benchmark-lab PR-927 is up as allowed-to-fail. Remaining: document rollout/rollback steps in ENG-4933 and update expected-behavior-b200-preview with strict pin requirement.
